Allocate

AL-uh-kayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To allocate is to distribute or assign for a particular purpose.

The relief agency will allocate most of its supplies to the villages hit hardest by the flood.

Worked Example

Before the road trip, Dad allocated forty dollars of the vacation fund to snacks and told us not to ask for more.

Dad set aside a specific share of the money for one particular purpose -- that act of assigning each portion its own job is what it means to allocate.

How Allocate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

assign

assign: to officially give out as a task or share

earmark

earmark: to set money or resources aside for one specific use

Antonyms

withhold

withhold: to keep back; to refuse to give

retain

retain: to keep for oneself instead of giving out

How Strong Is It? — give → allocate → earmark

give vs. allocate

give vs. allocate: To give simply hands something over -- to allocate adds a plan, deciding exactly which purpose each share will serve.

earmark vs. allocate

earmark vs. allocate: To earmark is even more specific than to allocate -- it locks one particular sum to one particular use, often officially.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — al-

prefix — al-: to, toward (a form of ad-) (Latin)

root — loc-

root — loc-: place (Latin (locus))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: verb-forming: to make or do (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Al- ('to') + loc- ('place') + -ate: to allocate is literally to place resources toward a purpose -- assigning each share its own place.

Root Check

Word Choice

Allocate is a practical, planning word -- you allocate money, time, staff, or supplies TO a purpose or person. Its tone is matter-of-fact: it describes careful assigning, not generosity or stinginess.
